items.t: Maple Ridge real estate market stats
Sell my house in Maple Ridge

Cottonwood is a named Maple Ridge neighbourhood in the City's own planning geography, listed among the Engage Maple Ridge neighbourhood names alongside Albion, Thornhill, Town Centre and Webster's Corners.
Cottonwood sits between the Town Centre to the west and the Kanaka Creek / Albion side of Maple Ridge to the east, on the Dewdney Trunk Road corridor toward Websters Corners.
What is confirmed is plan context: Cottonwood is inside the city-wide framework of Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, the same bylaw that governs secondary suites in zones including RS-1 and RS-2.

One secondary suite per lot is the Cottonwood rule under the city-wide summary: the suite must be inside the same building as the single detached home and must not exceed 40% of total Gross Floor Area (total floor area).

Secondary suites are permitted in zones the City lists as A-1, A-2, A-3, A-4, R-1, R-4, RS-1, RS-1a, RS-1b, RS-1c, RS-1d, RS-2, RS-3 and others — a Cottonwood buyer must confirm the lot's own zone in Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019.
A suite must not be in the Floodplain Area unless built above the established flood construction level, per the City's suite summary.

blocks.text: Cottonwood: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Kanaka Creek Regional Park runs about 11 kilometres up Kanaka Creek from the Fraser River to just south of Websters Corners, past the Albion side of Maple Ridge — the park corridor east of Cottonwood.
The City monitors Kanaka Creek levels during high streamflow events, along with the North and South Alouette and Fraser Rivers.
Sandbags for flood-prone Maple Ridge residents are made available at the City Operations Centre at 23925 Dewdney Trunk Road when risk increases.
A secondary suite must remain under the same legal title as the main home and cannot be used for short-term or vacation rentals, per the City's suite summary.

Maple Ridge's draft Capital Plan includes a 240 Street Bridge north of 124 Avenue as a second Alouette River crossing — a north-side project Cottonwood buyers watching Abernethy Way traffic should know is in pre-planning, not built.

The Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan was adopted January 27, 2026 (Official Community Plan Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021), directing most new housing and commercial growth around future Bus Rapid Transit stations at 203 Street, 207 Street, Laity Street and 216 Street — west of Cottonwood, on its commute corridor.
The City states the corridor plan does not itself change zoning or approve construction — a Cottonwood buyer should not treat a corridor designation as a building approval.
The Maple Meadows Park and Ride rate relevant to Cottonwood commuters is $3 daily and $60 monthly at 20010 Dunn Avenue.

Cottonwood's rapid transit link is the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus from Haney Place Exchange to Coquitlam Central Station, plus the future Langley–Haney Place Bus Rapid Transit line via the Golden Ears Bridge.
TransLink states the Langley–Haney Place Bus Rapid Transit service will connect to the future Surrey Langley SkyTrain at Willowbrook Station, the R3 RapidBus, and Carvolth Exchange and Park and Ride.
Maple Meadows Station (20010 Dunn Avenue, 435 spaces) is the West Coast Express Park and Ride for this side of Maple Ridge.

Check Kanaka Creek flood information first for low Cottonwood lots: the City's floodplain work states mapping will include minimum Flood Construction Levels for the Fraser River and parts of the Alouette River, with other systems to follow in 2027.
The City's flood material distinguishes creek flooding from river flooding — steep creeks such as Kanaka Creek can carry fast water, sediment and debris onto alluvial fans below.
Report blocked drains or debris to the City's 24-hour line at 604-463-9581 or MapleRidge.ca/Report, per the City's streamflow advisory — a useful number for a Cottonwood owner near a creek.

faq.a: The planned Langley–Haney Place Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) route shows the corridor logic for this side of Maple Ridge: it connects Maple Ridge with the Township of Langley via 200 Street, the Golden Ears Bridge and Lougheed Highway, over a 22-kilometre route with 13 stations. Drivers use the same Golden Ears Way / Golden Ears Bridge corridor south from the Lougheed Highway area.
